title: How can a still skip the frames before it?
answer: A still re-runs the scene on the same fixed clock and, unless the scene has updaters or is playing a Succession, skips computing the frames before t, so it matches playback whenever each frame depends on the time alone, and can miss when a frame depends on how many frames ran before it

checks.question: In the nudge version, the fade-in is stretched from 0.5 s to 1 s, so the move runs from t = 1 s to 2 s and the scene has 60 frames. Does the still at t = 1 s now match playback, and which is the first frame whose still differs?
checks.answer: The still at t = 1 s matches: frame 30 is now the last frame of the fade, and neither run has nudged the dot yet. The first frame that differs is 32. Frame 31 opens the move, and the seek and playback have each made one nudge there; by frame 32 playback has made two and the seek still one.

checks.question: Another version moves the dot by the change in time since the last frame it computed: x += distance × (α − α at the last frame). Does its still at t = 1 s match playback?
checks.answer: Yes. begin() computes α = 0, the skipped frames are never computed, and the frame at t = 1 s adds the whole change from 0 to 0.5 in one go, so the dot is halfway, as in playback. Keeping state is allowed, as long as the frame comes out the same however many frames ran before it.

checks.question: You write a typing animation: each computed frame appends the next character of a 60-character sentence, over a 2-second run at 30 fps. What does a still taken 1 s into that run show, and what change makes it match playback?
checks.answer: Playback has computed 30 frames by then and shows 30 characters; the still computes only the frame at t and shows about one. Show the first round(60 × α) characters instead, where α is the elapsed share of the run: each frame then depends on the time alone, and both show 30 characters at the midpoint.

scenarios.name: The dot moves by: Blending fixed endpoints

steps.title: Played, the dot is halfway at t = 1.00 s
steps.line: A still at t = 1 s skips computing frames 1–29. Where is its dot?
steps.caption: A direct link opens a later picture without playing the earlier steps, so Rayner makes that picture as a still. Here a box fades in, then a dot moves along a track. Rayner’s animate.moveTo moves the dot by blending its start and end. Playback has the dot halfway at t = 1 s. To make the still, Rayner re-runs the scene and counts frames 1–29 without computing them. Predict where the still’s dot will be before you go on.
steps.picture: Left: the tiny scene played: frame 30, t = 1.00 s, the dot halfway along its track, fingerprint ce5b0812. Right: an empty frame marked with a question mark, seeked: frames 1–29 only counted.

steps.title: The still matches: the same SVG, fingerprint ce5b0812
steps.line: Blending works the dot out from the time alone.
steps.caption: The pictures match because animate.moveTo calculates position from elapsed time and fixed endpoints. It does not need the earlier dot positions. A still re-runs the scene on the same fixed clock and, unless the scene has updaters or is playing a Succession, skips computing the frames before t, so it matches playback whenever each frame depends on the time alone, and can miss when a frame depends on how many frames ran before it.
steps.picture: Two frames of the tiny scene at t = 1.00 s, played and seeked, both with the dot halfway and the fingerprint ce5b0812.

steps.title: Seeked frame by frame, the nudged dot never passes its first step
steps.line: Line: where playback has the dot. Dots: a still taken at each frame.
steps.caption: Each panel plots the dot’s place on its track against the frame number, for all 45 frames of the tiny scene. The line is playback; each dot is a separate still, seeked to that frame. Through the fade, frames 1–15, the dot has not moved and the two agree. From frame 16 the dot moves: played, the blend eases in and out and the nudge climbs evenly, and both are halfway at frame 30, where the story took its still. A blended dot is placed by the frame’s time, so in this scene each still lands on playback’s line. A nudged still computes one frame of the move and makes one nudge, so its dots stay at the first step while playback climbs a nudge a frame. This scenario’s panel, on the left, has the bold title.
steps.picture: Two plots of the dot’s place on its track, start to end, against frames 1 to 45. Each has a line for playback and a dot for a still seeked to each frame. Blending fixed endpoints: every dot sits on the line. A nudge each frame: the dots follow the line through frame 16, then stay one nudge from the start while the line climbs to the end; at frame 30 playback has made 15 nudges and the still 1.

steps.title: Frame 30 is t = 1.00 s in every run
steps.line: Scene time is the frame number × 1/30 s, however fast the frames are taken.
steps.caption: The receiver of a frame is called a sink. A browser sink waits between frames; a trace sink can take them immediately. That changes how fast the output arrives, not the scene’s clock: both reach t = 1 s at frame 30. The target time therefore identifies the same frame even when earlier pictures are skipped.
steps.picture: Flowchart: 6 nodes, 5 links; 12 labels. Travelled: Fixed dt loop → Browser sink; Fixed dt loop → State trace.

steps.title: A frame is the shapes on stage, as the playing animations left them
steps.line: Once the still reaches frame 30, the playing animation decides where the dot is.
steps.caption: A Scene owns the shapes and text, called mobjects, and its animations change them. Rayner’s sinks only read the frame. The output cannot reconstruct missing nudges: the dot’s position must already be right when the animation hands over that frame.
steps.picture: Class diagram: 4 classes, 3 relationships; Beside Sink: it reads each frame and changes nothing. Travelled: Scene → Mobject: owns; Scene → Animation: plays; Scene → Sink: emits.

steps.title: An animation fixes its endpoints when it begins
steps.line: At t = 1 s the blend is halfway, however many frames ran before.
steps.caption: begin() copies the starting object. Each frame blends that copy with a fixed end by an amount set only by how far through its run time the animation is. Halfway through the duration therefore means halfway between the endpoints. In contrast, dot.shift(step) adds to the position accumulated by earlier frames.
steps.picture: Class diagram: 4 classes, 3 relationships; Code, 9 lines. Note: “endpoints fixed at begin()” beside Animation interpolate(). New in this step: Code, 9 lines.

steps.title: Seeked frame by frame: 45 of 45 match with blending, 16 with the nudge
steps.line: rayner check fails a page on the first seeked frame that differs from playback.
steps.caption: The strips compare each of those 45 stills with its played frame, the whole SVG, box and dot together. Blending agrees throughout; the nudge first differs at frame 17. rayner check samples less: in every step of every scenario it seeks one frame midway and one just before the step ends. A mismatch fails the check, but agreement at those two times proves nothing about the times between them. An updater follows a different path: in a scene with updaters, a still computes every frame before t.
steps.picture: Two rows of 45 cells, one per frame of the tiny scene, each comparing the seeked frame with the played one. Blending: all 45 match. A nudge each frame: frames 1 to 16 match, frames 17 to 45 differ. A line marks frame 30, the still at t = 1.00 s.
